edges.note: The commissioned question is how many unmanned vehicles a single human operator can control simultaneously - the human-factors constraint that would bound any swarming or multi-object control architecture. It forms a set with Genik's other two deliverables on limb-free control of external devices and on organic-molecule automation.

edges.label: author of record on the DIA list

It was written by the Toronto engineer who had run the Podkletnov replication and reported null results.

edges.label: subject domain: compact non-tokamak fusion power
edges.note: IEC is one of the few AAWSAP topics with a plausible conventional aerospace reading: a compact fusion device is what a small craft would need if it were producing the observed energy budget. The DIRD set contains four fusion-adjacent deliverables in total - Miley's IEC paper, Winterberg's advanced nuclear propulsion, Teofilo's aneutronic fusion propulsion for Lockheed Martin, and Culbreth's aneutronic fusion propulsion II.

edges.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Invisibility Cloaking, Dr Ulf Leonhardt, Univ of St Andrews.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Leonhardt had been publishing on transformation optics and cloaking since 2006 and was, by the ICOD of 1 December 2009, one of the small number of internationally recognised authorities in the field. George Knapp released a copy of the DIRD in February 2019.

edges.note: TIER 2 AND DELIBERATELY SO. The DIA list establishes at tier 1 that two aneutronic fusion DIRDs exist, one by V. Teofilo (Lockheed Martin) and one by W. Culbreth (UNLV). Which released document number belongs to which author is NOT stated on either cover, both of which redact the author under (b)(6). This document, DIA-08-1011-003, is assigned to Culbreth because the companion DIA-08-1011-004 carries a V. Teofilo self-citation at endnote 17 and Lockheed Martin content, while this one carries none of either and is instead saturated with Nevada Test Site, Project Rover and NERVA material plus nuclear engineering textbook citations. If the mapping is ever shown to be reversed, this edge and its partner must be swapped together.

edges.note: TIER 3, INFERENTIAL. AAWSAP was executed by BAASS out of southern Nevada, and BAASS subcontracted subject-matter experts to write the DIRDs. Culbreth was the University of Nevada, Las Vegas faculty member credited with two of them. No document in the public record states that BAASS specifically recruited him, and this edge should not be read as one.
